Shortage of teachers in schools
*61. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) what is the total shortage of teachers
in Primary to Higher Secondary, Group-
wise, in Government Schools in India as a
whole, State-wise, and Rajasthan in
particular as on date;
(b) whether the National Institute of
Educational Planning and Administration
has submitted any report in this context;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government have taken any
measures to do away with the shortage of
teachers in schools;
(e) if so, by when the shortage of
teachers is likely to be met; and
(f) what is the teacher-student ratio at
present and how does it compare with the
ideal ratio?
Scheme for girl education
*62. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have prepared
any special scheme/project for girl
education in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the names of the districts which are
covered under this scheme, especially in
Bihar and Maharashtra?
Drop-out rate of girl students
*63. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that number of
girl students who drop-out of schools at all
levels is uniformly and significantly higher
than that of boy students;
(b) whether Government have any
scheme underway that seeks to rectify this
anomaly;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

Development of National Disaster
Information System
*64. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL: Will the Minister of SCIENCE
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to develop a National Disaster
Information System (NDIS), which will
alert all citizens before any natural disaster
and terrorist attack through their mobile
phones, landlines and wireless;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) how long it will take to be functional;
and
(d) how far it will be useful in protecting
us in the event of any disaster?
Speedy disposal of criminal cases
*65. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have studied
the recent observations of the Supreme
Court of India  that around 1.77 crore
criminal cases are pending in various courts
across the country and that "Government
must take necessary steps immediately to
enforce the right to speedy trial of an
accused" which is one of the facets of the
fundamental right to life and liberty
enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution;
(b) if so, the results thereof; and
(c) the details of steps initiated to
liquidate this huge backlog and also for
speedy trial of cases to make the
administration of criminal justice effective,
vibrant and meaningful?
Intolerance and indiscipline in
campuses
*66. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
cognizance of growing cases of intolerance
and indiscipline in the campuses;
(b) whether Government have taken
steps to contain such cases of intolerance
and misbehaviour;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the steps
being taken to implement such steps
earnestly; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Rural electrification in Himachal
Pradesh
†*67. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH: Will
the Minister of POWER  be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of villages which have
been provided electricity by Government
during the last three years under the Rajiv
Gandhi Village Electrification Scheme in
Himachal  Pradesh;
(b) the amount provided under this
scheme and the names of the villages which
have been provided this facility so far;
(c) whether Government are considering
to provide some amount for Nandla village
of Chadhgaon Tehsil of Shimla district for
street-light; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

Tin reserve in Bastar forests
†*68. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that there are huge reserves of tin
in Bastar forests;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the slag
after smelting of tin is being purchased by
smugglers as it contains radioactive
elements like titanium, thorium and
uranium and thereafter smuggled alongwith
tin;
(c) whether it is also a fact that police
and flying squads of the corporation had
seized thirteen quintals of tin slag last year;
and
(d) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to check smuggling of these
items?
FDI in power sector
*69. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of POWER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that while 100
per cent FDI is allowed in power sector,
the holding companies governing such
projects cannot have more than 49 per cent
FDI;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether this anomaly has put on
hold substantial FDI;
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
projects affected by this; and
(e) the steps taken to remove this
anomaly?
Violence on domestic helpers
*70. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of
WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the incidents of violence on
domestic helpers are on rise in recent times;
(b) whether Government will agree to
conduct a nation wide survey on conditions
of minors engaged as domestic helpers; and
(c) the actions being taken for
rehabilitation of minors working as domestic
helpers?
Selling of children from 'Bal Sudhar
Grih'
†*71. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether incidents of giving on hire/
selling of children from 'Bal Sudhar Grih'
(Children Reform Homes) have come to
the notice of Government;
(b) if so, the details therefor;
(c) whether Government would make
arrangements for monitoring activities of
'Bal Sudhar Grihs'; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Population of Backward Classes and
SCs/STs
†*72. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the

23
55th Report of NSSO, the population of
Backward Classes was assessed as 34.5
per cent in 1999-2000;
(b) if not, the facts thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that in the
61st Report of the said organization, the
population of Backward Classes during
2004-05 has been indicated as 41 per cent;
(d) if so, the facts thereof;
(e) whether it is also a fact that in the
above-mentioned Reports, the said
organization did not mention any increase
in the population of SCs and STs; and
(f) if so, the facts thereof?
Rural Electrification in Andhra
Pradesh
*73. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 43.36 lakh
households and 13,000 habitations have
been identified in Andhra Pradesh for
electrification under Rajiv Gandhi Grameen
Vidyutikaran Yojana with an estimated cost
of Rs. 803 crores;
(b) if so, whether REC has sanctioned
schemes for 17 districts in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) if so, the details of districts and by
when the remaining five districts are going
to be covered under this programme;
(d) whether it is a fact that the
Government of Andhra Pradesh has been
requesting for releasing first  instalment to
implement RGGVY in 17 districts; and
(e) if so, the reasons for delay in releasing
first instalment to Andhra Pradesh?
Setting up of power plants
*74. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the details of power plants which
have been sanctioned and set up in the
country, particularly in the State of Sikkim
during each of the last three years;
(b) the details of funds allotted and spent
on the setting up of such plants in the
country during this period; and
(c) to what extent targets fixed in this
respect have been achieved?
New mining policy
*75. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a meeting of Chief Ministers
of States was held recently in Delhi;
(b) if so, the details of discussion held
in the meeting;
(c) whether some Chief Ministers have
serious doubts about the new mining policy;
and
(d) if so, the steps taken to clear their
apprehensions?
Abandoning of textbooks by NCERT
*76. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for abandoning the
'Science and Technology' series textbooks
of VI standard to X standard by NCERT;
(b) whether it is fact that the new science
book hurriedly prepared by NCERT for
VI standard is very rudimentary and very
much a backtrack of the previous 'Science
and Technology' book which was a bold
initiative to impart science to students in a

24

detailed and effective manner at the high
school level;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for diluting science education to
students at the crucial age; and
(d) the steps proposed to be taken to
review ineffective syllabus of science being
introduced by NCERT at high school level?
Targets for power generation
capacity addition
*77. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) the total capacity of power
generation (excluding captive generation)
in megawatt added during the Tenth Five
Year Plan period so far (break up of thermal,
hydel and other sources);
(b) the total capacity added in the
Seventh, Eighth and Ninth Five Year Plans
against the targets;
(c) the total capacity addition planned
in Eleventh Five Year Plan (excluding
captive generation);
(d) whether the same has been planned
based on existing rate of T & D losses;

(f) if not, the actual T & D losses based

planned?
School drop-outs in Jharkhand
†*78. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of drop-out boys and
girls between primary to secondary level
in Jharkhand, separately;
(b) the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps Government are taking to
reduce number of such drop-outs?
Use of energy saving CFLs
*79. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Bureau of Energy
Efficiency's audit of prominent Central
Government buildings has shown that
25-40 per cent energy could be saved each
year in these buildings with Compact
Fluorescent Lamps (CFLs); and
(b) if so, whether there is any proposal
to make mandatory the use of CFLs in place
of GLS bulbs in Government buildings to
save energy?
Loan for projects to tribals in
Jharkhand
*80. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether many tribals have been
given loans above Rs. five crores for starting
large projects in Jharkhand;
(b) whether there are any special training
schemes for tribals in Jharkhand to get self-
employed;
(c) if so, the details of institutions, the
number of beneficiaries, the type of skills
achieved during the last three years; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
